 Judgment
Dated this the 6th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.128/2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
For the purpose of convenience, the parties a 2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 17.3.2008.

According to the petitioner, on 17.3.2008 at about 11 a.m., while he was riding the motor cycle through Muringoor-Adichili public road, a tipper lorry having registration No.KL8-AC-1576, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motor cycle and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the 2025:KER:16355 petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.9,69,000/- (limited to Rs.5,00,000/-).
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A11, and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,01,760/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.

Heard Sri. P.V. Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt Raji T,
Bhaskar, the learned Standing Counsel 2025:KER:16355 for the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was a Plus Two Student.
The Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.3,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2008 will come to Rs.6,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the petitioner could not prove his income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6,500/- .
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"fracure shaft of (R) femu, type III open fracture of both bones, fracture of (R) little finger and compartment syndrome of leg and foot."
2025:KER:16355 13.
He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 69 days.
As per Exhibit A7 disability certificate issued by PW2, his permanent physical disability was assessed at 24.9%.

The Tribunal, however,
scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 20%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305). Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 24.9%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 18 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In 2025:KER:16355 the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.4,89,434/-.
15.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation for loss of education, as at the time of the accident the petitioner was a Plus Two student.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was inpatient for a total period of 69 days, I hold that towards 'loss of education' the petitioner is entitled to get the notional income for a period of three months, which will come to Rs.19,500/- (6,500x 3 months).
16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.15,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.500/- was awarded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 69 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on 2025:KER:16355 the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.50,000/-, Rs.30,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. The Tribunal has deducted 25% of compensation for the sole reason that the petitioner did not have a valid driving licence at the time of the accident.
In this case, the police registered a case in respect of the accident, against the 2nd respondent and Exhibit A3 is the charge sheet produced in this case.
As per Exhibit A3 charge sheet, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2nd respondent alone.
There is nothing to show that want of driving licence on the part of the petitioner has contributed to the accident.
In the above circumstances, the Tribunal was not justified in deducting 25% of the compensation for want of driving licence on the part of the petitioner.
Therefore, the said finding of the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.
20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.7,12,394/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

 4 Damage to clothing 500/- 500/-
 5

Medical Bills 1,05,610/- 1,05,610/-

 7 Pain and sufferings 25,000/- 50,000/-
 8 Loss of disability 1,42,800/- 4,89,434/-
 9 Loss of amenities 15,000/- 30,000/-
 Total 3,01,760/- 7,12,394/-
 Enhanced Rs.4,10,634/-
21.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.7,12,394/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Twelve Thousand Three Hundred and Ninety Four Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation,
with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

sentences.text: On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
23. In the Award, the Tribunal has permitted the 3 rd respondent to 2025:KER:16355 recover the compensation from respondents 1 and 2 as it found that the offending vehicle did not have valid permit.
I do not find any grounds to interfere with the above finding and as such the 3 rd respondent is permitted to recover compensation from respondents 1 and 2.
